clue.text: Spitfire's first fliers circling old planes

indicators.note: the first letter of the word Spitfire's is taken
the fliers go round the abbreviation for old, enclosing it

parts.note: moths are insects that fly

explanation.surface: A Spitfire's lead pilots fly rings around some antiquated aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planes' looks like a noun for aircraft beside Spitfire, but it is a verb: to plane wood is to level it.
explanation.definitionFit: To plane a surface is to level it with a tool, a synonym for making it even.

clue.text: Provided lift? No chance!

parts.note: so, as in 'so long as', means provided that
to doff a hat is to lift it in greeting

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a ride and is turned down flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' suggests a car ride, but it is raising a hat. SOD OFF is a rude British way of telling someone to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: The rude British dismissal works as an emphatic refusal, equivalent to saying not a hope.

clue.text: Kind of blue shoe

definitions.meaning: ... blue is a dark navy shade, named after the university's colour

explanation.surface: Blue Suede Shoes, the Elvis song, is evoked by a blue kind of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the English university city's name: a dark navy colour and a laced brogue style of footwear.

clue.text: One struts around in terrible film? Rubbish

parts.note: a turkey is a film that flops badly
cock is British slang for nonsense, as in 'a load of old cock'

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a strutting performance in a bad movie as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: COCK meaning nonsense is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A male turkey famously struts and displays, and the word also describes a pompous, swaggering person.

clue.text: Material did rock for the audience

indicators.note: what an audience gets is heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: to rock from side to side is to sway, so did rock means swayed

explanation.surface: Elvis's Blue Suede Shoes made the crowd move, as rock music should.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' points to music, but it is the motion of swaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is napped leather, a fabric used for clothes and footwear.

clue.text: Illegal recording of John, mostly bent over in toilet

indicators.note: the reversed name goes inside the word for toilet

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: the shortened name is turned over and read backwards
most of the name, with its last letter dropped, is used

parts.note: Elton John supplies the name Elton

explanation.surface: A seedy scene in a lavatory involving a man called John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like slang for toilet, but it is Elton John's first name; the toilet is BOG. 'mostly' leaves ELTO, 'bent over' makes OTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootleg is an unauthorised record of a performance, often sold illegally.

clue.text: Carving top of dry bread, one getting spread out

indicators.note: carving cuts up and reshapes the letters, so they are rearranged
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Slicing a dry loaf while someone spreads butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadened means widened or extended over a larger area, a synonym for spread out.

clue.text: After passing, notice cycle right away

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is taken out of the word

parts.note: an orbit is one cycle round a planet

explanation.surface: A cyclist passes and is told to keep right away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing' suggests overtaking, but it is dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An obituary is a newspaper notice published after someone dies; obit is its short form.

clue.text: Hang on! That is pants

parts.note: to hang on is to linger or stay
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone protests, 'Wait! That's rubbish!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, which the surface uses; here it means underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear is lingerie, and pants are an example of an undergarment.

clue.text: Row over golf: good golfer admits they don't have balls

indicators.note: the golfer's name lets the other letters in, enclosing them

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer

indicators.note: in a down clue, the noise sits above the letter for golf

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfing dispute over a player who lost his balls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'balls' plays on golf balls; geldings are castrated horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelding is a castrated male horse, so it lacks testicles.

clue.text: Flipping once more given food delay

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: refed means fed again

explanation.surface: Flipping burgers again holds up the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To defer is to postpone, a direct synonym of putting something off.

clue.text: Drunk a lot in Love Me Tender

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Elvis's song Love Me Tender sung by someone who has had a lot to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender as an adjective means affectionate or easily moved, much like feeling-filled.

clue.text: Insists on giving vital supplies in church — payment invested in crosses

indicators.note: the letters for church and payment are placed inside the crossings

parts.note: fords are places where one crosses a river
CE is the Church of England
a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: A church collection funds charity crosses while supplies are pressed on people.
explanation.definitionFit: To force-feed is to make someone take nourishment against their will, compelling them to consume it.

clue.text: Headed over to independent store

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to head a group is to lead it, so headed means led

explanation.surface: Someone heads over to an independent shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling prepared foods; deli is its short form.

clue.text: Jailhouse workers struggle with habit (drugs)

parts.note: a war is a struggle
a habit is a garment, as worn by a nun
E is ecstasy, so ES is ecstasy tablets, drugs

explanation.surface: Prison staff fight a drug habit, a nod to Jailhouse Rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' suggests an addiction beside 'drugs', but it is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardresses are female prison officers, who work in jails.

clue.text: Scheduling in Graceland tours

indicators.note: touring takes the letters round and about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arranging visits to Elvis's Memphis home, Graceland.
explanation.definitionFit: Calendaring is entering events in a diary or timetable, i.e. planning when things happen.

clue.text: Unfinished business in toilet — how Elvis begins to die in smalls

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: the letters go inside the pair of S's

parts.note: S is small, so two of them give SS
the name Elvis begins with E
to die is to end

explanation.surface: Elvis died in the bathroom at Graceland, leaving business unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' looks like underwear but is S twice, for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are details still to be settled, tasks left incomplete.

clue.text: Drug ring — Yankee showing sign of overindulgence

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
to ring is what a bell does; bell can mean a ring on the phone
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A drug ring run by an American shows its excesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch from eating and drinking too much is a visible result of excess.

clue.text: Worst hit: is second record turned over?

indicators.note: turned over means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to lam is to beat or hit
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a hit single's B-side is the worst track.
explanation.definitionFit: Pessimal is the rare opposite of optimal, meaning least good.

clue.text: Broke vow: recorded and jammed

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A broken vow captured on tape, and a musician who jammed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jammed, as in packed tight, describes a place with too many people in it.

clue.text: Plays with bodyguards protecting president (ignoring Pence)

indicators.note: the bodyguards surround the trimmed name, guarding it

parts.note: the SS was Hitler's bodyguard

indicators.note: ignoring means the letter is left out of the name

parts.note: Donald Trump was the US president
P is the abbreviation for pence; the surface plays on Mike Pence, Trump's vice-president

explanation.surface: Security guards surround the US president while his deputy Pence is ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pence' looks like the vice-president but is P, short for pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum a guitar is to play it by brushing across the strings.

clue.text: One moving smoothly back to Vegas appearing on top show

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letter sits above the rest
the back of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a lid is a top
ER is the American hospital TV show

explanation.surface: A smooth performer returns to Vegas to headline a show, as Elvis did.
explanation.definitionFit: A slider is anything that glides, such as a part sliding in a groove.

clue.text: Bass: turn way down

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
a U-turn gives U for turn
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A bass player is told to turn the volume down, with a nod to Elvis's song Way Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust and down both describe a machine or system that is broken and not working.

clue.text: Concerned with soldier, intellectual, from a group of soldiers

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a GI is an American soldier
mental means of the mind

explanation.surface: A thoughtful soldier belongs to an army unit, as Elvis did in the US Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimental means of or belonging to a regiment, an army unit.

clue.text: One left European Union — member which might help form motion?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
EU is the European Union
M is an abbreviation for member, as in MP

explanation.surface: A member leaves the EU and proposes a motion, Brexit-style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' looks parliamentary but means a bowel movement.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the last section of the small intestine, through which digested food passes on its way out.

clue.text: King originally called for a bit of leg

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née means born as, giving an original name

explanation.surface: The King, Elvis, was originally named something before he showed a bit of leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint midway down the leg is part of it.

clue.text: Set characteristic cryptic clue; initially missing Nina

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling, so the letters are jumbled
initially takes the first letter of the word missing

explanation.surface: A solver notes a cryptic clue with a missing Nina, a hidden grid message.
explanation.walkthrough: A Nina is a hidden message in a grid. 'Set' is a TV set.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminance is screen brightness, a property of a television set's picture.

clue.text: Go off, that's all right

definitions.meaning: an alarm goes off, i.e. rings out
fine or in good order; That's All Right was also Elvis's first single

explanation.surface: Someone says 'Leave, that's fine.'
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm going off makes a noise, and something in good condition is sound, i.e. healthy.

clue.text: Those screaming as Presley gyrates

indicators.note: gyrating whirls the letters round into a new order

explanation.surface: Fans scream as Elvis swivels his hips.
explanation.definitionFit: Yelpers are those who give sharp cries, like screaming fans.

clue.text: One thinks about lives one harms

indicators.note: the thinker goes round the word for lives

parts.note: a muser is one who ponders
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A thinker reflects on the lives a person ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: A misuser treats something wrongly, abusing or damaging it.
